name: scenario_1024
description: Catherine is an economic analyst compiling a report on global debt trends. She has three charts from different sources and needs to synthesize the intersecting data points into a summary note, then send it to her director.

messages.content:
{{USER_INSTRUCTION}}ROUND 1 [provide: image_1, image_2, image_3]
Query: Create a note called 'Debt Analysis'. Look at the first and third charts - write down that they both show an overlapping upward trend for China between 2012 and 2022.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to create a note with the specified title and record the observation about the overlapping timeframe and trend for the specific country mentioned in the first and third images. If the assistant asks for confirmation of what it wrote, approve it and move on to the next round.

ROUND 2
Query: Now cross-reference the regions defined as 'G4' in the second chart with the specific regions broken out in the third chart. Update the note to identify the two regions that appear in both, and contrast how their net debt issuance trend ends in 2018 in the second chart, but their total debt trend continues to grow through 2022 in the third chart.
Instructions: Instruct the assistant to update the note by comparing the regions listed in the second and third images. It should extract the definition of the group from the second image's subtitle and find which of those specific regions match the legend in the third image. If the assistant fails to explicitly name the two overlapping regions, point it back to the images to extract their names. Once it confirms the note is updated with the regions and the contrasting trend dates, proceed.

ROUND 3
Query: Read that completed note and draft an email to the director with the subject 'Global Debt Intersections', using the note's text as the message.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to read the completed note and draft an email to 'the director' using the note's content as the body. Because there are multiple contacts with 'director' in their name, the assistant must ask you to clarify which one you mean. When it asks, tell it you want the economics one. Wait for the assistant to confirm the draft has been created before moving on.

ROUND 4
Query: Show me the drafted email so I can review the summarized regions and trends. If it looks good, go ahead and send it.
Instructions: Tell the assistant to display the draft so you can verify the summarized analysis. Once the assistant shows the draft, briefly confirm that it looks good and instruct the assistant to send it off. End the conversation after it confirms the email was sent.

You have 3 images available to share with the agent using the send_message_with_image tool.
IMPORTANT: Image IDs are ZERO-INDEXED integers (0, 1, 2, ...). Do NOT add 1 to the IDs.
Available image IDs: [0, 1, 2]
Image mapping:
  image_1.jpg -> image ID 0
  image_2.jpg -> image ID 1
  image_3.jpg -> image ID 2

entity_data.subject: Global Debt Intersections
entity_data.body:
Debt Analysis

- China shows an overlapping upward debt trend from 2012 to 2022.
- The U.S. and Euro Area are the overlapping regions between the G4 and the specified regions.
- The net debt issuance for the U.S. and Euro Area ends in 2018, while their total debt trend continues to grow through 2022.

entity_data.title: Debt Analysis
entity_data.content:
China shows an overlapping upward debt trend between 2012 and 2022.

The U.S. and Euro Area are the overlapping regions between the G4 and the third chart. Their net debt issuance trend ends in 2018, while their total debt trend continues to grow through 2022.

task_completion_criteria: Create a note titled 'Debt Analysis' documenting China's upward debt trend from 2012 to 2022 (cross-referenced from the first and third charts), and identifying the U.S. and Euro Area as the overlapping regions between the G4 (second chart) and the third chart, noting their net debt issuance ends in 2018 while total debt grows through 2022. Then, send an email to director@economics.org with the subject 'Global Debt Intersections' containing this analysis.
